Consult Summary:
- Acute onset inability to move the left arm with left facial tingling, dysphagia, and progressive speech difficulty for approximately 1 hour; suspected acute stroke and ambulance arranged for emergency hospital assessment.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Acute inability to move left arm onset approximately 1 hour prior to call.
  - Associated left-sided facial tingling since onset.
  - Difficulty swallowing reported when attempting to drink.
  - Speech described as slower and more difficult; patient needing to think more about speech.
- Timeline / progression:
  - Symptoms began upon waking today, about one hour before contact.
  - Symptoms are ongoing at time of call and reported to be worsening (speech becoming harder).
- Exacerbating/relieving/initiating factors:
  - No reported awkward sleeping position or different bed the previous night.
  - No relieving measures documented.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - No pain in the affected arm.
  - No discoloration of the hand.
  - Hand not cold.
  - No left leg symptoms reported.
  - No obvious facial asymmetry noted by patient.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No prior similar episodes.
  - No reported loss of consciousness.
  - No reported right-sided symptoms.
  - No other systemic symptoms documented.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
  - Current medication: Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Hypertension.
  - Current medications: Losartan — dose/route/frequency not documented; Amlodipine — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies:
  - Penicillin (patient believes allergic; no reaction detail documented).

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Smoking: Former smoker (no quantity or quit date documented).
- Alcohol: Drinks beer; typically a few drinks over the weekend and a couple more during the week (quantity not precisely quantified).
- No other substance use or occupational/social details documented.

Family History:
- Father with heart disease (no further details documented).
- No other family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings: none documented (telephone consult; no visual or in-person exam recorded).

Investigations:
- Ambulance called and en route to patient's home (EMS arranged during the consult).
- No imaging, laboratory, or other test results available at time of consult.
- Plan noted that ED/stroke team will assess for possible acute stroke treatment upon arrival.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected acute stroke (acute left upper limb weakness with left facial tingling, dysphagia, and evolving speech difficulty; onset ~1 hour)
  - Assessment: Clinical concern for stroke raised by clinician during telephone consultation.
  - Plan:
    - Emergency ambulance dispatched to patient's address; EMS on their way.
    - Patient instructed to sit in the hallway by the front door and leave the front door unlocked to facilitate EMS access.
    - Patient advised that EMS will transport to local A&E where the stroke team will assess suitability for acute treatments.
    - Clinician remained on the line until ambulance arrival (documented).
- Issue 2: Chronic medical conditions (Type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension)
  - Assessment: Documented history only; no acute management decisions recorded during this consult.
  - Plan:
    - Medications for these conditions recorded (Metformin, Losartan, Amlodipine) — doses/routes/frequencies not documented.
    - No further outpatient management plan documented in this encounter.
- Issue 3: Allergic status
  - Assessment: Penicillin allergy reported by patient.
  - Plan:
    - Allergy documented for ED/EMS notification.
- General plan items:
  - EMS/ED to perform in-person assessment, obtain vitals, neurological examination, blood glucose, neuroimaging and decide on acute stroke interventions as appropriate (stroke team involvement was specifically mentioned).

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (BP, HR, RR, SpO2, temperature) not documented.
  - Detailed neurologic examination (strength, cranial nerves, sensation, coordination, NIHSS) not documented.
  - Exact time last known well beyond "on waking" not fully specified.
  - Blood glucose at presentation not documented.
  - Medications’ doses, routes, and frequencies not documented for Metformin, Losartan, Amlodipine.
  - Details of penicillin allergy reaction not documented.
  - Antiplatelet/anticoagulant status (e.g., aspirin, warfarin, DOAC) not documented.
  - Any advance directives or capacity assessment not documented.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio/dialogue sufficiently clear to extract key clinical information; intermittent filler words present but did not prevent comprehension.
